title: Mistral and Groq autologging: inject active span traceparent into SDK request headers, caller headers take precedence
answers: Why does my AI Gateway span not appear under the MLflow trace for a Mistral or Groq call?
Why is token usage counted twice when Groq requests go through the gateway with autologging on?
Does Mistral autologging overwrite a custom http_headers value I pass to chat.complete?
Where are the tracing headers merged into Groq extra_headers?
body:
Path: Autologging wrappers for Mistral chat.complete / complete_async (mlflow/mistral/autolog.py:patched_class_call, async_patched_class_call) and Groq chat.completions.create (mlflow/groq/_groq_autolog.py:patched_call). Every SDK call made while autolog is enabled passes through the per-file _inject_tracing_headers helper, including calls that already carry user http_headers or extra_headers.
Rule: Before calling the original SDK method, merge the header dict from mlflow/tracing/distributed.py:_get_tracing_headers_from_span(span) with the caller's dict as `tracing_headers | dict(existing)`, so caller keys win. Write the merged dict to a new kwargs entry (Mistral: `http_headers`, Groq: `extra_headers`) instead of mutating the user's dict. Do this after the span inputs are captured, so span.inputs keeps the user's headers and never shows traceparent. Wrap the merge in try/except with a debug log so header injection cannot break the SDK call.
Symptom: AI Gateway spans did not join the client MLflow trace, and the gateway's token usage was counted alongside the client span's usage, so totals were doubled.
Constraints: Injection happens only when a span exists and produces headers; Mistral's helper returns early when span is None. A custom user header (e.g. X-Custom) is preserved in the outgoing request. The traceparent sampling flag is not stored on the span, so tests compare only the trace and span IDs.
applies: Applies to mlflow/mistral and mlflow/groq autologging request paths; the same merge pattern fits any autologged SDK that accepts per-request headers.
says: Token usage counts are doubled when routing logged Groq requests through AI Gateway.
Gateway traces fail to connect to client traces during automated logging of model calls.
Automatic tracing overwrites custom HTTP headers supplied in Mistral chat completion requests.
Link AI Gateway call spans directly under the main application trace for autologged requests.
search: Autologging wrappers for Mistral and Groq must inject span traceparent headers into request kwargs while preserving caller-provided headers. Missing trace headers caused AI Gateway spans to detach from the client trace and led to doubled token usage counts. Header injection merges tracing headers into http_headers for Mistral and extra_headers for Groq after span inputs are captured, without mutating caller dicts.
